prompt: Use case: illustration-story. One original high-resolution master painting for a Sanskrit reader, part of a consistent 18-image Ishopanishad series. Square 1:1 canvas, request 2048 by 2048 pixels or the highest supported square resolution. Refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting. Use one coherent scene, no collage. Main narrative subjects MUST fit inside the central 60 percent of the width and central 50 percent of the height; surround them with generous low-detail sky, paper atmosphere and ground. Avoid important faces, hands and narrative objects near edges. This single master will be used behind live text in portrait and landscape on phones and tablets; surrounding atmosphere can crop, the scene must remain intelligible when fitted without cropping. Do not draw any Sanskrit, Roman text, verse numbers, typography, frame, border, watermark, infographic, UI, or page decoration. Do not portray a formless teaching as a specific deity unless the verse explicitly invokes that deity. Interpretive devotional illustration, not a literal historical reconstruction. Verse-specific source meaning from the app: All this, whatsoever moves on earth, is to be hidden in the Lord (the Self). When thou hast surrendered all this, then thou mayest enjoy. Do not covet the wealth of any man! Illustration: A single continuous landscape of river, trees, grazing deer, a tiny village and distant mountains, all gently permeated by the same subtle golden daylight. A modest person receives a small bowl of fruit with open hands while leaving the abundance of the living world undisturbed. Evoke divine pervasion, enjoyment with relinquishment, and freedom from coveting; no anthropomorphic deity.
